reporting-org.narrative: European Commission - Directorate-General for International Partnerships

title.narrative: European Union Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria EU-SDGN Phase III

description.narrative: Against the backdrop of democratic challenges in the West African region and the need to consolidate Nigeria¿s democratic experience as a regional leader, this new phase of the Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria (SDGN) aims to contribute to election-related reforms and initiatives for the second half of Nigeria¿s 2023-2027 electoral cycle with: i) support for the implementation of both the 23 recommendations made by the EU Election Observation Mission (EU-EOM) following its observation of the 2023 General Election, as well as the recommendations of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)¿s internal review; ii) strengthening media for democratic consolidation and combatting election-related information disorder; and iii) support for the efficient management of local government elections in selected states of the federation. The action will cover the February 2027 General Election as well as three off-cycle governorship elections and several by-elections. The action will draw on the lessons learned from the implementation of the current programme on democracy support.

title.narrative: i1.1.1a: Number of experts engaged by EUSDGNII to provide demandbased technical assistance, policy and expert advice to the Commission

description.narrative: i1.1.1a: Number of experts engaged by EUSDGNII to provide demandbased technical assistance, policy and expert advice to the Commission

comment.narrative: 25 senior experts deployed by EUSDGN II provided highlevel technical policy and strategic assistance to INEC Chairman and the Commission on several aspects such as on election security management electoral legal framework training and procedures political party campaign financing strategic communications and others. The technical assistance provided to the INEC Chairman and the Commission through the Technical Team and other senior experts was well received and highly appreciated by the INEC Chairman and the Commission and catalyzed various aspects of electoral planning and management.

title.narrative: i1.1.7a: Number of election observers trained and deployed by YIAGA Africa with support from the EUSDGN

description.narrative: i1.1.7a: Number of election observers trained and deployed by YIAGA Africa with support from the EUSDGN

comment.narrative: Yiaga Africa deployed the Process and Results Verification for Transparency PRVT methodology to observe three governorship elections in Benue Delta and Kano States. In total 900 trained stationary observers were deployed to a representative random sample of 300 polling units for each of the states and 97 roving observers. Yiaga Africa also trained and deployed 5 State Focal Persons SFPs and 92 Local Government Area LGA Supervisors in the three states.

description.narrative: i4.1.1c: Number of off cycle media round tables and engagement with stakeholders on election security

comment.narrative: Four 4 offcycle media roundtables and engagement with stakeholders on election security was jointly held by IPC and CEMESO for Kogi Bayelsa Imo and Edo offcycle governorship elections respectively. These activities comprised twoday media dialogueinterface sessions held for Bayelsa Aug 89 2023 Imo 1617 August 2023 Kogi 2829 August 2023 and Edo July 45 2024. This was complemented by media outreachlive programming sessions by CEMESO.

title.narrative: i5.2.2e: Web traffic on developed technology platforms for the election hub

description.narrative: i5.2.2e: Web traffic on developed technology platforms for the election hub

comment.narrative: In year one of the project TAF Africa Election Hub recorded a total of 1240 downloads. In year two however the TAF election observer App further enjoyed an additional 118 interactions with the public through downloads and eyewitnesses during the Kogi Imo and Bayelsa offcycle elections. The number of interactions recorded is mainly for the APP downloads. It is however noted that the backend web analytics for the TAF Election Hub was not factored into the design of the APP. Nevertheless TAF Africa is working on including this feature in the new improvement to take care of indicator demands.

title.narrative: i6.3.2b: Number of staff trained and deployed at Statelevel Situation Rooms

description.narrative: i6.3.2b: Number of staff trained and deployed at Statelevel Situation Rooms

comment.narrative: One hundred twenty 120 Staff were trained and deployed to track and report electoral conflict to the situation rooms. They were furnished with necessary knowledge and tools for prompt reporting to the situation rooms. Each of the 6 situation rooms and 15 conflict tracking observers received direct training on conflict tracking and early warning response as part of our electoral violence mitigation strategy. Further stepdown trainings were carried out for an additional 15 persons by the supervising situation room CSO making 30 deployed trackers on election day. However the directly trained officers served as daytoday conflict trackers for the respective situation rooms. A tracking Checklist was developed and familiarized by the trackers for ease of use.

title.narrative: i6.3.4d: Number of nonstate actors involved in a conference to manage electoral conflicts and violence

description.narrative: i6.3.4d: Number of nonstate actors involved in a conference to manage electoral conflicts and violence

comment.narrative: Three hundred and three 303 nonstate actors were involved in conferences 6 to manage electoral conflict and violence in the target states. During the conference participants were tasked with the responsibilities of developing and driving the implementation strategies that will promote peaceful conduct of elections in the States. Some of the strategies include facilitating awareness campaign advocacy visits to key EMB and other stakeholders to elicit their support etc. In Benue 44 participants attended the conference 36 attended in Borno 61 in Imo 59 in Kaduna 34 and 69 in Rivers and Oyo state respectively. This result have been achieved fully however we are followingup on participants to harvest and document outcomes. Some of the documented results include the strengthened engagement and collaboration by a coalition of nonstate actors Coalition of Civil Society in Peacebuilding in Rivers State. Following their participation at the conference in the state they met with the DG of the State NOA to elicit his support in their effort to promote peace and nonviolent elections in the State. Thereafter they were able to secure and utilize the agencys existing weekly program that is streamed live on social media Facebook to promote peace and women participation in elections. Similarly they had an engagement with the State Chairman of Labour Party following the outcome of the presidential elections to advocate for the peaceful conduct of their aggrieved members based on the outcome of the results. To this effect the aggrieved stakeholders in the party and state adopting constitutional means such as peaceful protest and litigation to express their grievances. Therefore ensuring the management of possible violent actions that would have erupted due to the action of some state actors that made efforts to jeopardize the electoral outcome.

title.narrative: i6.2.0e: Number of CBOs members that participated actively in grassroots stepdown trainings and have multiplier effects on their communities in 79 LGAs of Ekiti, Osun and Oyo in 2022 and 2023.

description.narrative: i6.2.0e: Number of CBOs members that participated actively in grassroots stepdown trainings and have multiplier effects on their communities in 79 LGAs of Ekiti, Osun and Oyo in 2022 and 2023.

comment.narrative: 927 CBO members participated actively in grassroots stepdown trainings and have multiplier effects on their communities in 79 LGAs of Ekiti Osun and Oyo. Generally these activities enhanced grassroots awareness of the need to collect PVC and active participation in the electioneering process by coming out to vote on the election day. Also an evident sense of belonging was demonstrated by trainees as more independent grassroots sensitizations were carried out by some trained NSAs and reported their activities on the WhatsApp group platform created for them by implementing organisations after the training.

title.narrative: i6.3.0b: Extent to which INEC takes measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

description.narrative: i6.3.0b: Extent to which INEC takes measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

comment.narrative: INEC sustained consultative meetings with security agencies and nonstate actors in Kaduna Benue Borno and Oyo states. Those consultative forums are geared toward improving the apparatus of the Commission that contribute to the peace of elections such as effective deployment of electoral materials early commencement of voting retraining and replacement of politically compromised or incapacitated adhoc staff for efficient election management.

title.narrative: i6.3.0c: Extent to which State agencies take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

description.narrative: i6.3.0c: Extent to which State agencies take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

comment.narrative: Kaduna State Peace Commission KSPC Ministry of Local Government Affairs MoLGA6 in Kaduna and Ministry of Women Affairs MoWA in Rivers State supported the mobilization of key stakeholders such as traditional leaders and women groups that participated in project activities in their States. KSPC also assigned senior staff members to cofacilitate the implementation of project activities in Kaduna. In a similar way National Orientation Agency NOA Rivers State chapter provided their Facebook channel to a coalition of nonstate actors Coalition of civil society in Peacebuilding for a livestreamed program7 to promote peace and women participation in elections. Furthermore statelevel electoral conflict tracking reporting and mitigation situation rooms in Benue Borno Imo Kaduna Rivers and Oyo States were established between December 2022 and January 2023 prior to the 2023 general elections. The situation rooms comprised of 6 CSOs representing one in each of the 6 project locations.

The situation rooms comprised of 6 CSOs representing one in each of the 6 project locations.

comment.narrative: Eight 8 youth groups in Borno Kaduna and Rivers State stepped down their knowledge in peacebuilding conflict resolution and citizens journalism eyewitness reporting to other members of their communities and volunteered to observe the 2023 general elections. The groups that contributed to this result are National Youth Council of Nigeria NYCN Rivers Advancing Youths in Agriculture ADYIA Rivers Niger Delta Youth for Democracy NDYD Rivers BUSHRA Glad Tidings Rivers Spinal Cord Injury Association of Nigeria SCIAN Kaduna Catholic Youth Organization of Nigeria CYON Kaduna YPM Borno and YAPPUMA Borno. The actions of these groups contributed to the reach of more members of their communities who served as agents of peace to promote nonviolent elections in the states as well as increase in youth participation during the electoral process.

title.narrative: i6.3.0d: Extent to which media actors and entities take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

description.narrative: i6.3.0d: Extent to which media actors and entities take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

comment.narrative: Nine 9 journalists reviewed their standard operational procedures to mainstream nonviolent reportage and improve their coverage monitoring and reportage of elections based on best practices. This contributed to their deliberate act of carrying out independent checks on information and claims before reporting. Thus contributing to the recorded minimal occurrences of violence during the 2023 general elections as against past elections in the target states. In addition Invicta FM in Kaduna state conducted stepdown training for 20 staff of the organization who are journalists on 23rd February 2023. Their action broadened the reach to other journalists while ensuring the transfer of knowledge on preventionmitigation of electoral conflictviolence.

title.narrative: i6.3.0e: Extent to which grassroot community leadership and structures take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

description.narrative: i6.3.0e: Extent to which grassroot community leadership and structures take measures to prevent/mitigate electoral conflict or violence in targeted States (measured by number, type and effectiveness of conflict/violence prevention or mitigation actions)

comment.narrative: Community leadership and structures in Borno and Kaduna states demonstrated commitment to peaceful and nonviolent conduct of elections in their communities through awareness creation and engagement with community security groups. For example in Borno state Jamaatu Nasril Islam JNI Maiduguri Chapter conducted rallies to create awareness on the importance of peaceful nonviolent free and fair election on major roads of the city such as Post Office Monday market and Baga Road. In addition Yerwa Patriot Movement YPM adopted doortodoor approach to sensitize members of their communities. In a similar way four 4 traditional leaders in Kaduna State held meetings with vigilante groups in their communities to sensitize them on the importance to maintain neutrality in their conduct before during and after the elections as their conduct could trigger violent conflicts within their respective communities.
